.._comment_prerelease: ADR-1201. The fork cuts release candidates before the final 1.0.0, so release-please publishes prereleases and GitHub marks them as such. `prerelease-type` fixes the channel at `rc`, matching the narrow tag pattern scripts/release/verify-release-version.sh accepts (vX.Y.Z-rc.N, no other identifier). ADR-1348: `versioning: prerelease` counts candidates (a fix, feature or breaking change on 1.0.0-rc.N gives 1.0.0-rc.N+1; `default` gave 1.0.1-rc.1). For the final cut flip `prerelease` to false: the same strategy then yields 1.0.0 with no version override. The release-script-contract gate requires `prerelease` versioning while the manifest carries a prerelease suffix, and enforces removal of the one-shot fields once it does not.
.._comment_changelog_notes: GitHub generates the release body from the merged pull requests rather than from commit subjects (ADR-1233). Sections come from .github/release.yml, which groups BY LABEL -- so .github/workflows/pr-type-label.yml derives a type:* label from each PR's Conventional-Commit prefix. Without that labeler every PR falls into the catch-all: 32 of the last 40 merged PRs carried no label at all. changelog-sections below still drives CHANGELOG.md, which is rendered from changelog.d fragments, so both surfaces stay meaningful.
